title: Spatial proteomics identifies lipid-droplet changes in Paramecium symbiosis
summary: Yan-Jun Chen and colleagues at Academia Sinica used spatial proteomics to compare the ciliate Paramecium bursaria and its algal symbiont under symbiotic conditions. The study reports symbiosis-associated shifts in lipid-droplet protein composition and localization, with microscopy and other measurements used to examine the interpretation. Spatial-proteome classification and condition-shift analysis helped identify the pattern; the study’s limited replicate count and possible co-fractionation of endoplasmic-reticulum material constrain interpretation.
ai_technology: SVM-based spatial localization and C-COMPASS condition-shift analysis of spatial proteomes
organization: Institute of Molecular Biology, Academia Sinica; Institute of Plant and Microbial Biology, Academia Sinica

evidence.tested: Spatial proteome profiles distinguished symbiotic conditions and implicated lipid-droplet-associated protein redistribution; microscopy and additional proteomic analyses provided supporting checks.
evidence.unknown: Three biological replicates per condition; possible ER co-fractionation remains a caveat, and the study does not establish all inferred functional consequences.
evidence.ai_role: SVM spatial localization and neural C-COMPASS analysis identify protein distributions and condition shifts in spatial proteomes.

source_review.scope: Primary source full text reviewed for title, authorship, Methods, Results, version date and stated limitations.
